correctness.rationale: The two dressed transition energies omega±=(omega1+omega2)/2±sqrt(delta²+lambda²) are distinct positive under lambda<sqrt(omega1 omega2), with mixing probabilities 0<q<p<1. Each dressed frequency forms two commuting two-state flips; summing stationary hot-contact flux yields the displayed channel currents. Their exact bath-swap difference is (g p q (p−q)/2)[omega− G(omega−/(2T))−omega+ G(omega+/(2T))], with G=U/(1+pq U), U=4 sinh²((1−1/k)x)/(sinh(2x/k)sinh(2x)). For phi(z)=z coth z, phi′,phi′′>0, so H0(x)=phi(2x/k)+phi(2x)−2phi((1−1/k)x) has H0(0)=0 and H0′>0. Since U decreases, H=H0/(1+pq U)=−xG′/G strictly increases. Therefore the log-ratio omega−G(omega−/(2T))/[omega+G(omega+/(2T))] strictly increases with inverse T. It tends to omega−/omega+<1 as T→infinity and infinity as T→0, proving unique crossing and its signs. Independent calculations verified the exact subtraction identity for several tuples and the example root ~0.7918074837, with 79 sampled monotonic inequalities; the analytic derivative is the universal proof.
residual_risks: Equal frequency-independent contact rates, exact global secular approximation and positive separated Bohr transitions are essential; resonance and lambda=0 destroy uniqueness.
Finite diagnostics do not prove all-temperature monotonicity.

originality.rationale: Upadhyay et al. (arxiv:2106.02891) study the locally phase-equivalent two-qubit DM hopping model and give the same stationary heat-current structure and opposing transition-frequency contributions (especially Eq.26). Their inspected results discuss rectification direction versus detuning but do not give the proved fixed-temperature-ratio all-absolute-temperature unique inversion law. Fogedby (2023) derives global heat currents and thermodynamic consistency; Khandelwal et al. optimize efficiency/rectification under other contact regimes. The contribution is the strictly monotone scalar ratio and exact global uniqueness, not the already known stationary current formulas.
residual_risks: A reformulation of existing two-channel rectification equations could implicitly establish this unique crossing in an uninspected appendix or old thermal-diode paper.
The local phase equivalence to DM hopping is acknowledged, so no novelty rests on rebranding the Hamiltonian.

value.rationale: For fixed two unequal qubits and fixed hot/cold ratio, the preferred diode orientation switches exactly once as only absolute temperature changes. This replaces a parameter-dependent numerical impression with a universal monotonic classification, gives one calibration temperature, and identifies the competing roles of two dressed heat-transfer channels. The result is a natural model-specific physical-mathematical invariant, not the mere computation of a sample current.
residual_risks: Does not address structured or unequal bath spectra, nonsecular dynamics, or reversal of heat flow against the gradient.

final_claim: For detuned exchange-coupled qubits, identical flat positive bosonic contacts and global secular Markovian dynamics, at every fixed k=T_hot/T_cold>1 there is exactly one positive common temperature scale T* at which the larger stationary hot-to-cold current magnitude switches bath orientation.
limitations: Flat equal g, detuning omega1>omega2>0, 0<lambda<sqrt(omega1 omega2), k>1, stationary global secular equation.
One current orientation switches, not the physical sign of heat flow.
